terms-of-service.lede: Draft for RMDHost review · Prepared 15 October 2026
terms-of-service.html:
Draft for review · 15 October 2026. These proposed policies require RMDHost approval before taking effect. Your accepted order and applicable mandatory law remain authoritative.

TermsPrivacyAcceptable useFair useSLACookies

1. Provider and scope

These proposed terms cover RMDHost virtual servers, dedicated servers, storage and game hosting. The contracting entity, registered address and applicable jurisdiction must be identified in the accepted order. For questions, contact support@rmdhost.com.

2. Orders and service descriptions

An order should identify the product, resources, location, billing currency, fees, support scope and any special commitments. A catalogue entry is subject to stock and confirmation. Services marked Coming Soon cannot be purchased through that entry. Third-party checkout sites have their own terms; review the identity of the seller before paying.

3. Accounts and access

Provide accurate account and billing details, keep credentials secure and notify support promptly about unauthorised access. You are responsible for people you authorise to use your account and for appropriate access controls on your services.

4. Billing and renewal

The order specifies billing frequency, renewal date and any setup or licence charges. Applicable taxes and the final total must be disclosed before payment. GBP estimates of USD list prices are indicative; the checkout currency and accepted total govern. Any payment failure, suspension or cancellation process must follow the accepted order and applicable law.

5. Permitted use and management

Follow our Acceptable Use Policy and Fair Use Policy. Unless management is included in the order, customers administer their software, patches, firewall, content and application configuration. Support availability does not mean software management is included.

6. Backups and customer data

Maintain independent backups and test recovery. If a plan includes backup, confirm its schedule, retention and restore procedure. File synchronisation, RAID and DDoS filtering are not substitutes for backup. On cancellation, export data before the service deletion date stated in your order.

7. Availability and incidents

Our network uptime commitment, service credits and exclusions are set out in the Service Level Agreement (100% Network Uptime SLA). Planned work, incidents and urgent security measures may affect availability as described there.

8. Cancellation and refunds

Use the client area or contact support to request cancellation. Confirm the effective date, renewal cutoff and data-export deadline. Refund eligibility, statutory cancellation rights and non-refundable third-party charges must be disclosed before purchase. No blanket refund window is established by this draft.

9. Abuse and suspension

We may need to restrict an affected service to address illegal activity, compromised systems or immediate harm. Where practical, explain the issue and give an opportunity to respond. Mandatory legal orders and urgent incidents may require action before notice.

10. Liability, disputes and changes

Any liability cap, exclusions and governing law require confirmation in the final agreement. Nothing in the final terms may exclude rights or liabilities that applicable law protects. Contact support first to attempt resolution. Material changes should be communicated before they take effect, with any required notice or cancellation rights.

privacy-policy.title: Privacy policy
privacy-policy.excerpt: Proposed RMDHost privacy notice describing account data, technical logs, support records, cookies, processors and individual rights.
privacy-policy.lede: Draft for RMDHost review · Prepared 15 October 2026
privacy-policy.html:
Draft for review · 15 October 2026. These proposed policies require RMDHost approval before taking effect. Your accepted order and applicable mandatory law remain authoritative.

TermsPrivacyAcceptable useFair useSLACookies

1. Who handles your data

RMDHost uses account and technical information to operate hosting services. The final notice must identify the legal controller and its address. Privacy enquiries can be sent to support@rmdhost.com. Hosting customers may separately act as controllers for data they store on their servers; an appropriate processing agreement is needed where we act as processor.

2. Information involved

Depending on how you interact with us, information may include name, contact and billing details, order history, transaction references, IP addresses, security logs, device or browser details, support correspondence and consent preferences. Avoid sending passwords or unnecessary sensitive information in tickets. Payment processors handle payment credentials under their own notices.

3. Purposes and legal grounds

Account setup, provisioning, billing and support are needed to perform the service contract. Security and abuse prevention may rely on legitimate interests, subject to applicable safeguards. Accounting and lawful disclosures may be legal obligations. Where required, optional analytics or marketing relies on consent. The final notice must match actual tools and processing.

4. Sharing and third parties

Infrastructure providers, payment processors and support or communications providers may receive the information necessary for their role. Information may also be disclosed where legally required. External supplier checkout and account websites are operated separately; review their privacy notices before using them. The final notice must identify relevant recipient categories and processing arrangements.

5. Cookies and external resources

Read the Cookie Policy and use cookie settings to manage optional consent. The website may request external fonts, which can disclose IP and browser information to the font provider. Disabling optional analytics does not remove necessary service or security processing.

6. International transfers

Server and service locations can involve processing outside your country. Confirm provider locations, subprocessors and any legally required transfer mechanism before moving personal data. This draft does not certify a particular transfer safeguard or residency commitment.

7. Retention and security

Keep personal information only as long as necessary for its purpose, legal obligations or disputes. Specific retention periods, backup deletion cycles and account-deletion procedures must be confirmed in the final notice. Access controls, encryption where appropriate and incident procedures reduce risk but cannot eliminate it.

8. Your rights and requests

Depending on applicable law, you may request access, correction, erasure, restriction or portability, object to processing or withdraw consent. Contact support@rmdhost.com; identity verification may be needed. Rights can have legal exceptions. You may also complain to the competent data protection authority, including the ICO where UK law applies.

9. Children and notice changes

These services are intended for people able to enter the relevant service contract. If a child has supplied personal information without appropriate authority, contact us. The final policy must explain material changes and its effective date.

acceptable-use.title: Acceptable use policy
acceptable-use.excerpt: RMDHost Acceptable Use Policy: what you may and may not do with our VPS, dedicated, game, edge and storage services, and how we handle abuse reports.
acceptable-use.html:
TermsPrivacyAcceptable useFair useSLACookies

1. Scope

This Acceptable Use Policy (AUP) applies to every RMDHost service, including VPS, dedicated, game, edge and storage services, and to everyone who uses them through your account. It forms part of our Terms of Service. You are responsible for all activity on your services, including activity by your users, customers and anyone who gains access to them.

2. Illegal and harmful content

You must not host, store, transmit or link to: child sexual abuse material (reported to the authorities immediately); malware, ransomware or exploit kits intended for unauthorised use; stolen data, credentials or payment cards; phishing pages or fraudulent shops; content that infringes copyright, trademarks or other rights; content that incites violence or terrorism; or any other material that is illegal where it is hosted or where it is aimed.

3. Network abuse

You must not use our network to: launch or sell DDoS attacks, “stressers” or “booters”; scan ports or probe other networks without the owner’s permission; spoof IP addresses or forge packet headers; break into or interfere with any system; operate botnet command-and-control servers; or run open resolvers, open proxies, open relays or other services that can be abused for amplification. Security testing is allowed only on systems you own or have written permission to test.

4. Email and spam

You must not send unsolicited bulk email or messages, or host websites advertised through spam. Mailing lists must be opt-in, include a working unsubscribe link and honour requests promptly. Purchased, rented or scraped lists are not permitted. If an IP address is blocklisted because of activity on your service, you must fix the cause before we request delisting.

5. Resource use

Use resources within your plan and our Fair Use Policy. Cryptocurrency mining, proof-of-space farming and similar sustained full-load workloads are not permitted on VPS, cloud or game server plans without our written approval; they are allowed on dedicated servers. Do not try to get around plan limits, licence checks or account restrictions.

6. Game servers

Game servers must follow the game publisher’s end-user licence and server rules. Do not host cheat distribution, account trading fraud or stolen game assets. Mods, plugins and maps must be properly licensed. Attacks on other game servers, including from your own players, must be reported to us and stopped.

7. Your security responsibilities

Keep operating systems and software up to date, use strong passwords or SSH keys, close ports you do not need and remove unused accounts. If your service is compromised, you must clean it up promptly. We may help, and we may restrict the service until it is safe.

8. Copyright and complaints

Send copyright notices and other complaints to support@rmdhost.com with the affected URL or IP address, the material concerned, evidence of your rights and your contact details. We forward valid complaints to the customer responsible and may remove access to clearly unlawful material.

9. How we enforce this policy

When we receive a credible report or detect abuse, we usually contact you first and give you a reasonable time to fix the problem. For serious or ongoing harm, such as active attacks, malware, phishing or child abuse material, we may null-route an IP address or suspend the service immediately. Repeated or severe breaches can lead to termination under our Terms of Service. We co-operate with law enforcement where the law requires.

10. Reporting abuse

Report abuse to support@rmdhost.com. Include the IP address or domain, the date and time with timezone, logs or headers showing the activity, and how we can contact you. Please do not include passwords or other secrets.

fair-use.title: Fair use policy
fair-use.excerpt: Proposed fair-use rules explaining shared CPU, unmetered bandwidth, player slots and resource-impact reviews.
fair-use.lede: Draft for RMDHost review · Prepared 15 October 2026
fair-use.html:
Draft for review · 15 October 2026. These proposed policies require RMDHost approval before taking effect. Your accepted order and applicable mandatory law remain authoritative.

TermsPrivacyAcceptable useFair useSLACookies

1. Meaning of plan limits

Plan allocations and the accepted order define available CPU, RAM, storage, traffic and ports. Shared resources must be used without materially disrupting other customers. This policy does not change explicitly purchased dedicated allocations.

2. Unmetered is not unlimited speed

Unmetered traffic usually means no stated per-GB billing within the selected port and contract conditions. It is not a promise of uninterrupted line-rate throughput. A port speed, traffic quota and network mitigation capacity are separate specifications.

3. CPU, storage and workloads

Sustained CPU contention, excessive disk I/O, full storage or unusually high packet rates can affect a shared platform. Tell sales about continuous heavy processing, public proxies, high-traffic delivery or similar workloads so suitability can be confirmed before ordering. No arbitrary CPU percentage or daily limit is imposed by this draft.

4. Game-server capacity

Unlimited player slots does not mean unlimited CPU, RAM or guaranteed performance at every player count. Mods, map size, tick rate and simultaneous players influence resource demand. Review the selected game package before inviting a large community.

5. Review process

When activity affects platform stability, support should explain the measured impact and discuss optimisation, an upgrade, traffic controls or a different service. Urgent harm may require temporary restrictions. Any permanent restriction or extra charge must have a contractual basis.

6. Questions and related rules

Ask support@rmdhost.com to confirm suitability for an unusual workload. See the Acceptable Use Policy for prohibited activity and the Terms of Service for contract terms.

sla.title: Service level agreement
sla.excerpt: RMDHost Service Level Agreement: a 100% network uptime SLA with service credits for downtime, covering VPS, dedicated, game, edge and storage services.
sla.html:
TermsPrivacyAcceptable useFair useSLACookies

1. Our commitment

RMDHost provides a 100% Network Uptime SLA. Our network is built to keep your service reachable at all times. If network downtime affects your service, you are entitled to a service credit under this agreement. This Service Level Agreement (SLA) forms part of our Terms of Service.

2. Covered services

This SLA covers active, paid services in good standing: Linux, Windows, SSD, Cloud and Lightsail VPS; dedicated servers, including instant dedicated servers; game servers; edge servers; and OwnCloud storage servers. Services marked Coming Soon, trials and free services are not covered until they are paid and active.

3. What counts as network downtime

Network downtime is a period when the public IP address of your service cannot send or receive traffic because of a fault in the RMDHost network: our routers, switches, uplinks, power or cooling. Downtime starts when our monitoring detects the fault or you report it, whichever is earlier, and ends when connectivity is restored. Problems inside your server, such as the operating system, applications or firewall rules, are not network downtime.

4. Service credits

For each network downtime incident, you receive a credit worth a percentage of the monthly fee of the affected service:

Network downtime in one incidentService credit
Up to 15 minutes5% of the monthly fee
15 minutes to 1 hour10% of the monthly fee
1 to 4 hours25% of the monthly fee
4 to 12 hours50% of the monthly fee
More than 12 hours100% of the monthly fee

Credits for all incidents in one calendar month are capped at 100% of that month’s fee for the affected service.

5. Exclusions

No credit is due for downtime caused by: scheduled maintenance announced at least 72 hours in advance; emergency maintenance needed to fix a security vulnerability; your own actions or software, including misconfiguration, reboots and resource exhaustion; hardware failure inside a dedicated server (hardware is replaced as quickly as possible and handled separately); suspension under our Terms of Service or Acceptable Use Policy; null-routing needed to protect our network from an attack aimed at it rather than at your service; problems on networks outside our control, such as your users’ internet providers; or events beyond our reasonable control (force majeure).

6. How to claim a credit

Open a support ticket or email support@rmdhost.com within 14 days of the incident. Include the service ID, the affected IP address, the start and end time of the downtime with timezone, and any evidence such as monitoring alerts, ping or MTR results. Never include passwords. We check the claim against our network monitoring and reply within 5 working days.

7. How credits are paid

Approved credits are added to your account balance and used against your next invoice for the affected service. Credits are not paid in cash and cannot be transferred. If you cancel the service, unused credits expire. Service credits are your sole remedy for network downtime under this SLA, without affecting any rights you have by law.

8. Maintenance and status updates

We plan maintenance to avoid busy hours and announce scheduled work at least 72 hours in advance by email. Live service health is shown on our network status page.

9. Related documents and changes

Read this SLA with our Terms of Service, Acceptable Use Policy and DDoS protection details. We may update this SLA from time to time; changes do not reduce the credit for an incident that happened before the change.
